I couldn't manually smoke-test the running server — this session has no approval surface for background/multi-step bash commands, so those were auto-denied (not run, not failed). The unit tests I added (`test/serve.test.js`) exercise the actual HTML rendering logic including the streak count and HTML-escaping, and the full suite passes (10/10).

**Summary of changes:**
- `src/serve.js` — new module: `serve(port = 4321)` starts an `http` server (Node built-in, no new dependency) that renders an HTML table of habits and current streaks on every request; `renderHtml()` is exported separately for testing.
- `src/cli.js` — wired up `habit serve [port]`.
- `test/serve.test.js` — covers streak rendering, HTML escaping, and the empty-habits case.

Usage: `node src/cli.js serve` (default port 4321) or `node src/cli.js serve 8080`.
